hypothesis: Adding bounded exact-token search over reviewed change evidence, with matched terms and an explicitly named rawRelevance score, will let hosts retrieve relevant provenance without mislabeling ranking output as semantic similarity or confidence.
heldOutChecks: a query for raw retrieval ranking finds the Ruflo score-semantics correction first
every result exposes exact matched terms and rawRelevance equal to matched unique query terms divided by unique query terms
results are deterministic, sorted by rawRelevance and then reviewed feed order, without similarity or confidence fields
project and kind filters are exact, intersect with the query, and do not alter score semantics
CLI and MCP return equivalent search results and enforce bounded hostile-input handling
a no-match query returns an empty result set without semantic inference or fallback claims

memoryDecision.exactBaseline: exact project/kind filtering and chronological change paging
memoryDecision.candidate: explainable exact-token retrieval with no learned weights
memoryDecision.ruvectorWasm: defer until at least 100 sanitized provenance records support leakage-free exact, vector and fused comparisons
memoryDecision.gnn: reject unless a held-out graph task demonstrates at least ten percentage points of task-success gain over exact retrieval and a shuffled-graph control

forecast.prediction: Within 90 days, agent-memory retrieval interfaces will increasingly distinguish raw retrieval relevance from downstream ranking or confidence and expose enough match provenance to audit threshold behavior.
forecast.falsifiableCriterion: By 2026-12-17, at least two primary agent-memory implementations or interoperability specifications newly publish separate raw-relevance and ranking/confidence fields plus regression tests or threshold semantics.
